raw_response_text:
{
  "project_id": "P-IND-ChhattisgarhAcceleratedLearning",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "Heatwaves, erratic monsoons, and climate-induced disasters may cause extended school closures and reduce annual instruction days.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Integrate climate adaptation and disaster risk management (DRM) training for principals, adopt disaster-resilient school designs, and implement digitally enabled diagnostic assessment tools.",
      "evidence": "The state is vulnerable to droughts and floods due to erratic monsoons and heat waves that can force extensions of the annual school summer break..."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "Adolescent boys in secondary and senior secondary grades face economic pressures to drop out of school to take up informal labor or farm work.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Prioritize targeted remedial education, expand access to senior secondary science and commerce streams, construct residential facilities for boys, and engage communities via SMCs.",
      "evidence": "...given the limited access to quality science and commerce education, adolescent boys in secondary and senior secondary grades find it economically beneficial to drop out..."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "Shortage of subject-specialized teachers due to fiscal constraints leads to non-subject teachers delivering mathematics, science, and English instruction.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Develop and distribute structured grade- and subject-wise lesson plans and transition to a need-based, customizable in-service teacher professional development system.",
      "evidence": "Further, a lack of subject teachers in schools managed by the GoCG has resulted in Language teachers teaching Mathematics, English, and Sciences."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "Lack of periodic state achievement surveys and diagnostic assessment data limits the ability of education institutions to identify and remedy learning gaps.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Institutionalize periodic State Level Achievement Surveys (SLAS) and deploy centrally designed, digitally enabled school-based diagnostic assessments with automated remedial plans.",
      "evidence": "The lack of a standardized system to assess student learning through a diagnostic lens restricts the nodal educational institutions’ ability to identify issue(s)..."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "High prevalence of small, fragmented primary/upper primary schools leads to multi-grade teaching and high per-pupil operating expenditures.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Transform existing facilities into at least 600 model composite schools operating with economies of scale, dedicated subject teachers, and semi-autonomous management.",
      "evidence": "...fragmented school functioning have led to multi-grade teaching and higher per-pupil expenditure."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "Capacity and human resource constraints at SCERT, SAC, and SIEMAT may impede the execution of multi-year teacher training, assessment, and leadership initiatives.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Engage technical support agencies, specialized consultants, and a PMC under the IPF component to build institutional capacity and support implementation.",
      "evidence": "However, the SAC has limited capacity and experience in these areas."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "Multiple planning tiers and limited budgeting capacity among executing agencies cause delays in budget approvals and fund releases, leading to lower execution rates.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Conduct a financial management study, streamline planning processes, roll out a multi-tier FM training module, and deploy a PMC to assist with AWP&B preparation.",
      "evidence": "...capacity gaps pertaining to the preparation and management of budgets often result in inadequately planned budgets and consequent delays in fund releases and low budget execution rates."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "Internal control weaknesses, including inadequate control over advances and unresolved statutory audit observations dating back to FY 2009-10, create financial management risks.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Establish an internal control monitoring cell, create an Audit Committee, update internal audit terms of reference, and organize district/block camps to clear past audit observations.",
      "evidence": "there exist unresolved/ addressed statutory observations since FY 2009-10."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "Lack of annual procurement planning, absence of standard procurement templates, and non-disclosure of contract award data introduce procurement inefficiencies and governance gaps.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Mandate annual procurement plan preparation, incorporate World Bank Anti-Corruption clauses into contracts, conduct independent procurement audits, and publish award notices on e-GP platforms.",
      "evidence": "...the assessment found that there is no practice of preparing an annual procurement plan with timelines or of public disclosure..."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "Inexperience of SIS-SS staff with World Bank Procurement Regulations could cause procurement processing delays for consultancy packages under the IPF component.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Assign experienced procurement staff, mandate the use of the STEP system, apply Standard Procurement Documents, and provide extensive World Bank handholding and training.",
      "evidence": "Procurement risks related to the IPF component include the inexperience of the SIS-SS to process consultancy services following World Bank Procurement Regulations..."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "Civil works for model school infrastructure may result in occupational health and safety hazards, community safety risks, construction dust/noise, and improper waste disposal.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Incorporate standardized EHS obligations in bidding documents, perform environmental risk screening for all civil works, enforce National Disaster Management guidelines, and implement waste management plans.",
      "evidence": "Environmental risks and impacts associated with... dust and disposal of construction waste... Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) and Community Health and Safety (CHS) issues..."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "Overcrowding in tribal hostels and geographical barriers in remote areas threaten equitable access to quality secondary education for ST and SC students.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Conduct secondary infrastructure needs assessments, establish residential facilities for boys and teachers in topographically complex areas, and prioritize model school development in tribal/backward blocks.",
      "evidence": "...over-crowding of students in tribal hostels, lack of geographic and needs-based planning to ensure equity and access, especially among tribal and backward areas..."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R13",
      "description": "The gradual transition away from coal mining over the next 20 to 30 years threatens local employment and necessitates workforce reskilling for youth in mining blocks.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Establish at least 5 percent of composite model schools in coal mining blocks to provide senior secondary science and commerce education that enables a just economic transition.",
      "evidence": "...gradual closure of coal mines that produce 85 percent of the country's coal over the next 20 to 30 years. There will be a need for reskilling/upskilling..."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R14",
      "description": "Weak institutional capacity for environmental and social supervision and inadequate grievance redress escalation channels could lead to unaddressed local social or environmental impacts.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Appoint dedicated E&S experts within SIS-SS, strengthen the grievance redress mechanism with clear escalation protocols, and implement community-led school social audits.",
      "evidence": "key social risks... emerge from weak institutional capacity for E&S activity implementation... need for strengthening grievance redress mechanism for a system of escalation..."
    }
  ]
}
